rules.description: Portable extinguisher inspection — seven-item check: in place, visible, accessible, gauge in operable range, full by heft, hose/nozzle condition, tamper seal intact
rules.automation_note: Permitted by electronic monitoring since the 2007 edition. IFC §906.2 Exc. 2 goes further and is the richest credit in the code: thirty-day inspections not required AND maintenance allowed once every 3 years — dry-chemical/halogenated only, indoors, on a listed and approved device. TRAP: §7.2.1.4 — monitoring for LOCATION ONLY (a bracket removal switch) does NOT excuse the manual inspection. Monitoring must sense pressure, presence and obstruction.
rules.residual_human_step: NFPA 10 §7.6.1.2 — 100% of monitoring units verified annually (tightened from a 20%/year rotation), plus §7.6.2 semiannual NFPA 72 visual inspection of the monitoring devices themselves. Automation creates new human work.
rules.record_retention: Electronic event log at the control panel — NFPA 10 §7.2.4.6

rules.description: Emergency lighting — functional test, minimum 30 seconds (min 3, max 5 weeks between tests)
rules.automation_note: Computer-based self-testing automates BOTH the 30-day 30-second test and the annual 90-minute test. Critically, §7.9.3.1.3 contains NO 30-day human visual inspection — unlike §7.9.3.1.2, which does. The difference between those two subsections is worth real money.
rules.residual_human_step: None. This is the only obligation found where the code fully deletes both the periodic and the annual manual test.
rules.record_retention: Written records kept by the owner — NFPA 101 §7.9.3.1.1(5)

rules.description: Emergency lighting — functional test, minimum 1.5 hours (90 minutes) at full load
rules.automation_note: Computer-based self-testing performs the annual 90-minute test automatically and must report full test/failure history on demand (§7.9.3.1.3(5)). UL 924 self-test hardware ships today.
rules.residual_human_step: None for the test itself. Note the limit: a fixture aimed at a wall passes its own 90-minute self-test perfectly — illumination LEVEL along the egress path (1 fc avg / 0.1 fc min / 40:1) is a photometric survey of a space, not a self-test of a fixture.
rules.record_retention: Written records kept by the owner

rules.description: Sprinkler control valve inspection — normal position, sealed/locked/supervised, accessible, correct wrenches, free from external leaks, identification
rules.automation_note: SUPERVISION DISCOUNT. Sealed valves: weekly. Locked OR supervised per the applicable NFPA standard: monthly (4x). Electrically supervised: quarterly. No AHJ approval, no performance-based programme, no listing of automated ITM equipment — just supervision plus a monitored receiving point. Two gating conditions: NFPA 72-grade supervision (integrity-supervised circuit, supervisory signal, trouble on fault), and connection to a CONSTANTLY ATTENDED LOCATION. A hotel front desk is staffed 24/7 — the hard condition is satisfied for free.
rules.residual_human_step: The inspection CONTENT of §13.3.2.2 still applies at the reduced frequency. Annual full-range valve operation under §13.3.3.1 is untouched.
rules.record_retention: One year past next ITM of that type

rules.description: Fire pump no-flow (churn) test — start by pressure drop, run, record suction/discharge pressure, RPM, volts, amps, packing gland drip
rules.automation_note: One of the strongest rows in the permission map. Verbatim: "Qualified personnel shall be in attendance whenever the pump is in operation UNLESS automated inspection and testing is performed in accordance with 8.3.2.10." Weekly for diesel, monthly for electric.
rules.residual_human_step: §8.3.2.10.2 — all checklist observations still performed and abnormalities recorded. §8.3.2.10.2.2 — if packing gland adjustment is indicated, qualified personnel must make it. §8.3.2.10.3 — diesel controller must have automatic engine shutdown.
rules.record_retention: One year past next ITM of that type

rules.description: Water storage tank heating system — inspection during the heating season
rules.automation_note: THE LARGEST SINGLE DISCOUNT IN NFPA 25. Daily during the heating season becomes weekly where the tank has a supervised low water temperature alarm connected to a constantly attended location — approximately 7x.
rules.residual_human_step: The supervised alarm itself becomes an inspected device.
rules.record_retention: One year past next ITM of that type

rules.description: Fire alarm control unit inspection — fuses, interfaced equipment, lamps and LEDs, primary power
rules.automation_note: A 52x credit already built into the inspection table and widely unnoticed: a MONITORED system inspects control equipment annually; an UNMONITORED system inspects the same items WEEKLY. Monitoring is not merely good practice — the code prices it.

rules.description: Fire alarm manual test frequency — extended to annually where automatic weekly testing is performed by a remotely monitored, listed control unit
rules.automation_note: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS THE UL LISTING, NOT THE CODE. Three gating conditions: testing must be automatic and at least weekly; performed BY the fire alarm control unit, not a bolt-on IoT overlay; and the FACU must be "specifically listed for the application." That phrase means the credit accrues to the PANEL MANUFACTURER, not an aftermarket sensor vendor. The provision has stood since ~2007 and nobody has commoditised it. NOTE: NFPA 72 contains NO self-testing clause — zero hits across the 2022/2025/2028 committee corpus. Vendor claims describe UL 268 listings.
rules.residual_human_step: Table 14.3.1 visual inspection frequencies are untouched by this credit.
rules.record_retention: Until the next test and 1 year thereafter — NFPA 72 §14.6.2.1

rules.description: Main drain test — record static pressure, open the 2-inch drain fully, record residual, close, confirm return to static
rules.automation_note: Mechanically the most automatable procedure in NFPA 25: two transducers and a motorised valve. The test is literally "record two numbers and compare to baseline," and the 10% criterion is arithmetic. Detects a closed or obstructed supply valve upstream — the deadliest failure in the building.
rules.residual_human_step: Frequency unchanged (§4.6.6.12). Discharge visually observed at least once every 3 years (§4.6.6.4.2).
rules.record_retention: One year past next ITM of that type

rules.description: Waterflow alarm test — vane, paddle and pressure-switch type. Must signal within 90 seconds
rules.automation_note: Automated equipment MAY perform the test (§4.6.6.3 — it must produce the same action the standard requires). But §4.6.6.12 is explicit: frequencies are maintained REGARDLESS of the functionality of automated testing equipment. On the water side, automation buys labour substitution and evidence quality — not fewer events.
rules.residual_human_step: NFPA 25 §4.6.1.1 — automated testing shall be observed at a minimum frequency of once every 3 years. §4.6.6.14 — results analysed by qualified personnel.
rules.record_retention: One year past the next ITM of that type — NFPA 25 §4.3.5

rules.description: Firefighter Emergency Operation (FEO) — Phase I recall and Phase II in-car operation test
rules.automation_note: SECTION NUMBER UNVERIFIED — ASME A17.1 is paywalled and absent from the Public.Resource corpus. The monthly frequency is near-universally reported by elevator contractors and AHJs; treat the frequency as reliable and the section number as a lead. Phase I recall automates. PHASE II DOES NOT: the entire test is "does the car obey a firefighter continuously-pressed thumb" — constant-pressure door close, release at halfway to force reversal, constant-pressure open, CALL CANCEL. There is no way to test constant-pressure behaviour without a constant pressure. A relay that simulates the button proves the relay works, not the safety.
rules.residual_human_step: Phase II in its entirety. Elevator inspection is state-licensed almost everywhere — the one item a hotel can essentially never self-perform.
rules.record_retention: Certificate posted in the car, renewed annually

rules.description: Fire-resistance-rated construction — owner visually inspects, and maintains an inventory of rated construction
rules.automation_note: Underrated and widely skipped. An explicit ANNUAL, OWNER-PERFORMED duty covering all rated construction, plus a requirement to maintain an inventory of it. Most hotels do not do this — and an asset graph is exactly an inventory of rated construction.
rules.residual_human_step: Concealed firestopping is a person with a flashlight above a ceiling tile, forever. Cameras plus change detection do catch path obstruction well.

rules.description: Commercial kitchen hood wet-chemical suppression — inspect and test for proper operation; service within 6 months and after any activation
rules.automation_note: NFPA 17A does not yet permit remote ITM at all — there is no technology answer here. The procedure is a chain of mechanical states: cable tension through pulley elbows, nozzle aim, blow-off cap age, cartridge weight, detection-line integrity, fusible links. Instrument the OUTCOME states and accept a two-hour hands-on semiannual. The 3-dollar tension-lever switch that catches "left it UP" after service is worth more than the rest combined.
rules.residual_human_step: The entire semiannual service. Certificate of inspection to the fire code official.
rules.record_retention: Certificate to the fire code official

rules.description: Extinguisher maintenance — thorough physical examination, internal/external exam, hose and nozzle, recharge if needed
rules.automation_note: Maintenance is a hands-on teardown by a certified person who applies a tag. Automation can displace INSPECTION (§7.2); it cannot displace MAINTENANCE (§7.3). The only relief is IFC §906.2 Exc. 2, which stretches this to 3-yearly under five conditions.
rules.residual_human_step: Full annual external exam by a certified person; 6-year internal; 5/12-year hydrostatic. Tag hand-punched with the technician name and company.
rules.record_retention: Tag remains on the extinguisher; records until next annual + 1 year

rules.description: Drills of the hotel emergency organisation
rules.automation_note: A hard recurring calendar obligation that is NOT a device test — a staff event with a record. Frequently missed, and it belongs in any hotel compliance calendar.
rules.record_retention: Hilton brand standard: current calendar year + previous 6 years

rules.description: Emergency power supply system — weekly inspection of the generator and appurtenant components
rules.automation_note: RELIEF WAS REFUSED IN WRITING. Public Inputs 18 and 21 in the 2022 cycle asked for relief at unmanned sites; Resolution FR-15 granted it only to Level 2 systems on reduced criticality. Generators already telemeter heavily — Table 5.6.5.4 has a remote-audible column — and still require the walk-up. A modern controller senses nearly every weekly checklist item, which makes this a pure regulatory blocker rather than a technical one.
rules.residual_human_step: The weekly physical walk-up. Monthly 30-minute load run at 30% nameplate or the manufacturer exhaust gas temperature.
rules.record_retention: Records: date, technician, conditions noted, corrective action — IFC §1203.4.3

rules.description: Backflow prevention assembly — forward flow test at system demand
rules.automation_note: The physics is easy — permanent transducers on the test cocks plus a motorised needle valve would run the whole RPZ sequence. The obstacle is the LICENSING REGIME: in most jurisdictions only a certified backflow tester with an annually calibrated gauge may sign the test, and the WATER PURVEYOR, not the fire AHJ, owns the requirement. Non-filing can terminate water service. Continuous relief-port discharge detection is worth deploying today regardless — it catches a fouled check the day it fouls rather than eleven months later.
rules.residual_human_step: The signed annual test, by a certified tester, filed with the water purveyor.
rules.record_retention: Filed with the water purveyor annually

rules.description: Fire pump annual flow test — churn, 100% and 150% of rated capacity
rules.automation_note: No automated path absent permanent test loops. The hose-stream or flowmeter-to-drain arrangement is required at least every third year.
rules.record_retention: One year past next ITM of that type

rules.description: Fire door assembly inspection — eleven checkpoints including label legibility, no field modifications, clearance, closer, latch, coordinator, glazing, gasketing, hardware
rules.automation_note: Two of the eleven checkpoints automate cleanly — self-close and latch verification, via a position encoder plus a strike-plate latch-engagement sensor. They happen to be the two that fail constantly and the two that actually stop smoke. The other nine are irreducibly tactile at ~220 leaves in a 150-key hotel: a technician runs a HAND over the leaf and finds the filled-and-sanded hole a camera reads as paint. CAUTION: networked door closers and strike-plate latch sensors are already patented — freedom-to-operate review required.
rules.residual_human_step: Nine of eleven checkpoints, per leaf, annually. Record signed by the inspector of record.
rules.record_retention: Acceptance for the life of the assembly; otherwise at least 3 years

impairments.threshold_citation: NFPA 25 §15.5.2(4). Zurich classifies this as a HIDDEN impairment — an outage existing without the knowledge of those responsible. Continuous valve-position monitoring collapses this category to zero.

candidates.mechanism: Imaging sweep with change detection against the last sweep
candidates.verdict: THE central hard problem. Categories are subtle — factory white vs a fresh coat of the same white. Best play deletes the SWEEP, not the JUDGEMENT. Anyone claiming full automation here is selling something.
A technician runs a hand over the leaf and finds what a camera reads as paint. Clearance measurement is a genuine unbuilt sensor opportunity.
You cannot test constant-pressure behaviour without a constant pressure. Accept it.
A fixture aimed at a wall passes its own self-test perfectly. Monitor for regression, do not claim to measure compliance.
Sensing is solved outright. ACCESS is not — many are drywalled or painted shut. Capture at renovation, one floor at a time.
The 3-dollar tension-lever switch is worth more than the rest combined.

candidates.item: dBA at the pillow, door closed
candidates.verdict: Ambient moves with the PTAC, the ice machine, the cart, the guest TV. And the walkthrough is where technicians find water-stained tiles.

candidates.mechanism: Transducers on the test cocks plus a motorised needle valve
candidates.verdict: Blocked by the licensing regime, not physics. Deploy relief-port discharge detection today regardless.
You cannot prove a hose valve opens under fire conditions without opening it. Irreducible.

candidates.item: Firestopping and "has a human broken something"
candidates.mechanism: Cameras plus change detection for path obstruction
candidates.verdict: The state space of ways to break a building is unbounded. Concealed firestopping is a person with a flashlight above a ceiling tile, forever.

candidates.mechanism: Absolute stem-position encoder replacing the binary tamper switch
candidates.labour_note: ~2 hr/yr — but it is not about the hours
candidates.verdict: Upgrades "someone turned it" to "it is 78% open and has been since March." The highest-consequence failure in the building becomes continuously visible. A safety argument, not a labour one.

candidates.mechanism: UL 924 self-test hardware with a reporting layer
candidates.labour_note: ~9-12 hr/yr of button-pressing plus a weekend of 90-minute breaker work
candidates.verdict: The code fully deletes both tests. Batteries are the #1 failure and a runtime self-test catches them precisely.
Ride it in on the same network.
Converts a coin-flip into a measurement. Voltage-only checks produce false passes.

candidates.mechanism: Read the value the panel already computes, nightly
candidates.verdict: Nothing to invent. The addressable panel already computes it.
NOT A CODE ITEM AT ALL — no AHJ, no listing, no standard. The shortest path from sensor to dollars, and it funds the code lanes.
Produces better evidence than a technician with a stopwatch and a radio — exact seconds to signal, exact gpm.

candidates.mechanism: Two transducers and a motorised valve
candidates.verdict: The most mechanically trivial procedure in NFPA 25.

candidates.mechanism: Transducers in place of or parallel to analog gauges
candidates.verdict: Kills the "gauge stuck at zero for three years" failure.

candidates.mechanism: Optical gauge read, weighted hook, tamper and obstruction sensing
candidates.verdict: The code did the hard part.

candidates.item: Generator weekly and monthly run data
candidates.verdict: Technically solved; the weekly walk-up was refused relief in writing.

candidates.mechanism: Solenoid, transducers, tachometer, optical drip counter
candidates.verdict: Every number on the clipboard is instrumentable.

candidates.mechanism: Position encoder plus strike-plate latch sensor
candidates.verdict: Two of eleven checkpoints — the two that fail constantly. PATENTED: freedom-to-operate review required.
Solved everywhere except on rated doors in hotels.

candidates.mechanism: Reconcile panel log against central-station log
candidates.verdict: Both sides are already digital. Today it is a phone call and a hope.
